lessons.name: the turn carries the feeling and loses none of it: two feelings that are the same after the turn were the same feeling
lessons.statement: ∀ f : Feel, ∀ g : Feel, Episode.turn (feel f) = Episode.turn (feel g) → f = g

lessons.name: feel is defined: a feeling is exactly one valence and one arousal, core affect (Russell 2003, doi 10.1037/0033-295X.110.1.145), so there are 4 feelings, 2 valences by 2 arousals, and feel f is the episode that feeling begins at the feeling corner
lessons.statement: (∀ f : Feel, feels.contains f = true) ∧ feels.length = 4 ∧ (∀ f : Feel, (feel f).corner = .feeling ∧ (feel f).feel = f)

lessons.name: flipping a feeling's valence keeps its arousal and its corner, undoes itself, and commutes with the turn on every episode
lessons.statement: ∀ e : Episode, (Episode.turn e).flip = Episode.turn (Episode.flip e) ∧ Episode.flip (Episode.flip e) = e ∧ (Episode.flip e).feel.arousal = e.feel.arousal ∧ (Episode.flip e).corner = e.corner

lessons.name: what a feeling turns into: feel f, turned, is a thought reading the same feeling, turned again an emotion completing it, and turned 3 times it is the feeling again
lessons.statement: ∀ f : Feel, Episode.turn (feel f) = ⟨.thought, f⟩ ∧ Episode.turn (Episode.turn (feel f)) = ⟨.emotion, f⟩ ∧ Episode.turn (Episode.turn (Episode.turn (feel f))) = feel f

lessons.name: the valence flip acts on every corner at once, leaving each corner where it is, and commutes with the turn: σρ = ρσ on every state
lessons.statement: ∀ a : Affect, (Affect.turn a).flip = (Affect.flip a).turn ∧ (Affect.flip a).corner = a.corner

lessons.name: the valence flip, pleasant ↔ unpleasant (Russell 1980, doi 10.1037/h0077714), undone by itself and fixing neither valence: σ² = id
lessons.statement: ∀ v : Valence, Valence.flip (Valence.flip v) = v ∧ Valence.flip v ≠ v

lessons.name: turning and flipping together has order exactly 6, so the 6-element group is cyclic: ℤ/3 × ℤ/2 ≅ ℤ/6, and the lens is abelian, not the triangle's dihedral symmetry
lessons.statement: (∀ a : Affect, iter (fun b => (Affect.turn b).flip) 6 a = a) ∧ (List.range 5).all (fun k => states.map (iter (fun b => (Affect.turn b).flip) (k + 1)) != states) = true

lessons.name: the turn and the flip generate a group of exactly 6 elements, 3 turns times 2 flips (ℤ/3 × ℤ/2): the closure of the identity under both holds the identity, is closed under each generator, and has 6 action tables on the 6 states
lessons.statement: (∀ a : Affect, states.contains a = true) ∧ generated.contains states = true ∧ generated.all (fun t => generated.contains (t.map Affect.turn) && generated.contains (t.map Affect.flip)) = true ∧ generated.length = 6

lessons.name: the loop runs feeling → thought → emotion → feeling: a feeling, the body's raw affect signal, is read by a thought, the appraisal (Lazarus 1991, doi 10.1037/0003-066X.46.8.819; Scherer 2009, doi 10.1080/02699930902928969), and the reading completes an emotion, the whole episode of affect joined to a concept (Barrett 2017, doi 10.1093/scan/nsw154), which is felt again
lessons.why: a corner of the lens: feeling, the body's raw affect signal; thought, the appraisal that reads it; emotion, the whole episode, affect joined to a concept -/ inductive Corner where | feeling | thought | emotion deriving DecidableEq /-- valence, the pleasant–unpleasant axis every corner carries (Russell 1980, doi 10.1037/h0077714) -/ inductive Valence where | pleasant | unpleasant deriving DecidableEq /-- a state of the lens: one corner carrying one valence -/ structure Affect where corner : Corner valence : Valence deriving DecidableEq /-- a property holds of every corner exactly when it holds of the 3, so a universal over corners decides by checking each -/ instance (P : Corner → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ c, P c) := decidable_of_iff (P .feeling ∧ P .thought ∧ P .emotion) ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1, h2⟩ x => by cases x <;> assumption, fun h => ⟨h _, h _, h _⟩⟩ /-- the same for the 2 valences -/ instance (P : Valence → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ v, P v) := decidable_of_iff (P .pleasant ∧ P .unpleasant) ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1⟩ x => by cases x <;> assumption, fun h => ⟨h _, h _⟩⟩ /-- and for the states: every corner with every valence -/ instance (P : Affect → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ a, P a) := decidable_of_iff (∀ c, ∀ v, P ⟨c, v⟩) ⟨fun h a => by cases a; exact h _ _, fun h _ _ => h _⟩ /-- ρ, the turn: feeling → thought → emotion → feeling, each corner 120° from the next -/ def Corner.turn : Corner → Corner | .feeling => .thought | .thought => .emotion | .emotion => .feeling /-- ρ⁻¹, the loop run backward -/ def Corner.back : Corner → Corner | .feeling => .emotion | .thought => .feeling | .emotion => .thought /-- σ, the valence flip -/ def Valence.flip : Valence → Valence | .pleasant => .unpleasant | .unpleasant => .pleasant /-- the turn and the flip lifted to the states: each moves its own coordinate and leaves the other -/ def Affect.turn (a : Affect) : Affect := ⟨a.corner.turn, a.valence⟩ def Affect.flip (a : Affect) : Affect := ⟨a.corner, a.valence.flip⟩ /-- arousal, the calm–charged axis of the body's signal -/ inductive Arousal where | calm | charged deriving DecidableEq /-- the same decision for the 2 arousals -/ instance (P : Arousal → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ x, P x) := decidable_of_iff (P .calm ∧ P .charged) ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1⟩ x => by cases x <;> assumption, fun h => ⟨h _, h _⟩⟩ /-- a feeling, the body's raw affect signal: core affect, one valence and one arousal (Russell 2003, doi 10.1037/0033-295X.110.1.145) -/ structure Feel where valence : Valence arousal : Arousal deriving DecidableEq /-- a property holds of every feeling exactly when it holds of every valence with every arousal -/ instance (P : Feel → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ f, P f) := decidable_of_iff (∀ v, ∀ a, P ⟨v, a⟩) ⟨fun h f => by cases f; exact h _ _, fun h _ _ => h _⟩ /-- an episode: the corner it stands at, and the feeling it began from -/ structure Episode where corner : Corner feel : Feel deriving DecidableEq /-- a property holds of every episode exactly when it holds of every corner with every feeling -/ instance (P : Episode → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ e, P e) := decidable_of_iff (∀ c, ∀ f, P ⟨c, f⟩) ⟨fun h e => by cases e; exact h _ _, fun h _ _ => h _⟩ /-- feel f: the episode a feeling begins, standing at the feeling corner -/ def feel (f : Feel) : Episode := ⟨.feeling, f⟩ /-- the turn on episodes carries the feeling to the next corner; the valence flip turns the feeling's valence and keeps its arousal and corner -/ def Episode.turn (e : Episode) : Episode := ⟨e.corner.turn, e.feel⟩ def Episode.flip (e : Episode) : Episode := ⟨e.corner, ⟨e.feel.valence.flip, e.feel.arousal⟩⟩ /-- the 4 feelings, listed -/ def feels : List Feel := [⟨.pleasant, .calm⟩, ⟨.pleasant, .charged⟩, ⟨.unpleasant, .calm⟩, ⟨.unpleasant, .charged⟩] /-- a point of the drawn lens: one of the corners, or the centre they turn around -/ inductive Point where | corner (c : Corner) | centre deriving DecidableEq /-- a property holds of every point exactly when it holds of every corner and of the centre -/ instance (P : Point → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Decidable (∀ p, P p) := decidable_of_iff ((∀ c, P (.corner c)) ∧ P .centre) ⟨fun ⟨h, h'⟩ p => by cases p <;> first | exact h _ | exact h', fun h => ⟨fun _ => h _, h _⟩⟩ /-- the turn on points: each corner to the next, the centre to itself -/ def Point.turn : Point → Point | .corner c => .corner c.turn | .centre => .centre /-- the plane in Eisenstein coordinates: (a, b) is a + bω, ω a primitive cube root of unity; the turn is multiplication by ω, exact on integers -/ def rot (p : Int × Int) : Int × Int := (-p.2, p.1 - p.2) /-- each corner drawn at ω to the power of its place in the loop -/ def coord : Corner → Int × Int | .feeling => (1, 0) | .thought => (0, 1) | .emotion => (-1, -1) /-- the lattice points within 3 of the centre on both coordinates -/ def span : List Int := (List.range 7).map (fun i => Int.ofNat i - 3) def box : List (Int × Int) := span.flatMap (fun a => span.map (fun b => (a, b))) /-- f applied n times -/ def iter {α : Type} (f : α → α) : Nat → α → α | 0, a => a | n + 1, a => iter f n (f a) /-- the 6 states, listed -/ def states : List Affect := [⟨.feeling, .pleasant⟩, ⟨.feeling, .unpleasant⟩, ⟨.thought, .pleasant⟩, ⟨.thought, .unpleasant⟩, ⟨.emotion, .pleasant⟩, ⟨.emotion, .unpleasant⟩] /-- one round of the closure: every table reached so far, carried by the turn and by the flip, kept if new -/ def grow (seen : List (List Affect)) : List (List Affect) := seen.foldl (fun acc t => [t.map Affect.turn, t.map Affect.flip].foldl (fun acc' u => if acc'.contains u then acc' else acc' ++ [u]) acc) seen /-- the group the turn and the flip generate, as action tables on the states: the identity grown 3 rounds -/ def generated : List (List Affect) := iter grow 3 [states] /-- the loop runs feeling → thought → emotion → feeling: a feeling, the body's raw affect signal, is read by a thought, the appraisal (Lazarus 1991, doi 10.1037/0003-066X.46.8.819; Scherer 2009, doi 10.1080/02699930902928969), and the reading completes an emotion, the whole episode of affect joined to a concept (Barrett 2017, doi 10.1093/scan/nsw154), which is felt again

lessons.name: the observer is the fixed point of the turn, not a corner: on the drawn lens the turn moves every corner and leaves only the centre where it is; in the plane, with the corners at 1, ω and ω² in Eisenstein coordinates and the turn multiplication by ω, the corners follow the loop and sum to the centre (1 + ω + ω² = 0), and of the 49 lattice points within 3 of the centre the rotation fixes exactly one, the centre
lessons.statement: (∀ p : Point, Point.turn p = p ↔ p = .centre) ∧ (∀ c : Corner, rot (coord c) = coord (Corner.turn c)) ∧ ((coord .feeling).1 + (coord .thought).1 + (coord .emotion).1 = 0 ∧ (coord .feeling).2 + (coord .thought).2 + (coord .emotion).2 = 0) ∧ box.all (fun p => (rot p == p) == (p == (0, 0))) = true ∧ box.length = 49

lessons.name: the loop also runs backward: ρ⁻¹ undoes the turn on either side, and running back once is turning forward 2 times, ρ⁻¹ = ρ²
lessons.statement: ∀ c : Corner, Corner.back (Corner.turn c) = c ∧ Corner.turn (Corner.back c) = c ∧ Corner.back c = Corner.turn (Corner.turn c)

lessons.name: 3 turns of 120° return every corner to itself: ρ³ = id, so the loop closes
no turn short of a full loop (ρ¹, ρ²) leaves any corner where it was: the observer is the axis the loop turns around, not a fourth corner it lands on
lessons.statement: ∀ c : Corner, Corner.turn c ≠ c ∧ Corner.turn (Corner.turn c) ≠ c
